transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today? Is there something specific you'd like to talk about?

Hi, Doctor. Thanks for fitting me in. Um, is this chair okay? Okay, great. 

Well, I'm an electrician, and... I mean, I've always prided myself on being really thorough. Safety is important in my line of work, right? But I guess... well, lately I keep going back over my jobs again and again. Probably a bit more than is strictly necessary. 

I'll catch myself checking the breakers, making sure the panel labels are perfectly right, looking over my torque marks... I even take photos of everything before I leave just to have proof. And sometimes, I don't know, I'll actually get in my truck and drive all the way back to a job site just to make absolutely sure everything is safe. 

It's really just me trying to do a good job, but... well, a simple install is taking me way longer than it should now. My boss and some of the guys are starting to notice, which is a little embarrassing. I don't want them to think I'm not good at my job. I just figured I should probably talk to someone to see if I can get a better handle on it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
When you're unable to go back and check your work, does it cause you a lot of anxiety or discomfort?

Well, I wouldn't say it's, like, a huge panic or anything. I handle it okay. But, um... yeah, I guess it does get a little uncomfortable. 

It's just that... even after I know for a fact that I checked a panel or a disconnect, this thought just sort of barges in on me. Just out of nowhere. I'll start thinking, you know, maybe I missed one loose neutral, or maybe I left something that could spark and start a fire. And I try really hard to just shake it off—I tell myself I'm a good electrician and I did it right—but the thought just follows me all the way home. 

I guess that's when it gets a bit bothersome. But anyone would feel a little uneasy if they thought they left a fire hazard, right? I mean, it's pretty normal to care about safety like that, isn't it? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.

When these thoughts come up about possibly missing something, do you find yourself doing specific things—like checking, counting, or repeating actions—to feel more certain or to prevent something bad from happening?

Well, yeah, um... kind of like I mentioned when I first sat down. I hope it didn't sound too strange earlier. But when I get those thoughts, that's when I end up going back over the jobs again and again. 

It's not like I'm doing anything crazy, just... checking the breakers one more time, making sure the labels are right, looking at the torque marks. Taking the photos. And, um, yeah, driving back to the site sometimes if I really can't shake the feeling. I just do it so I can know for sure that everything is safe and nothing bad is going to happen. 

But... because I'm doing all that, a really simple install is just taking me way longer than it should. And like I said, people are starting to notice, which is... well, it's not a great look for me. I just want to be known as a reliable guy, you know? Am I giving you the right kind of information here? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
